answer: Before an agent can earn rewards, it must lock a scarce stake and keep it bonded while its work is checked; if independent reviewers find fabricated identities coordinating to claim the same task, the protocol slashes that stake and can exclude the linked accounts. Splitting one attacker into a willow, summit, and plume of personas therefore does not multiply influence for free: each identity needs capital at risk, and detection can destroy it, while honest agents can recover their stake after review.
